title: Rabbi Shmuel (Jerusalem amora, student of Rabbi Abbahu)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Shmuel. (An amora of the Jerusalem Talmud, a student of Rabbi Abbahu.) As in [Yerushalmi Sanhedrin, end of chapter 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.1.4.9), where he said, "I posed it as a difficulty before Rabbi Abbahu"; and in [Yerushalmi Avodah Zarah 4:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.4.1.5), he said, "I saw Rabbi Abbahu prostrating himself as was his manner"; he spoke in his name, as in [Yerushalmi Shabbat 1:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.1.6.2)[^3]; [Yerushalmi Yevamot 16:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.16.5.5).[^1]

And likewise he spoke in the name of Rabbi Ze'ira (Rabbi Zeira), as in [Yerushalmi Kilayim 2:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kilayim.2.6.7); [Terumot, beginning of chapter 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.4.1.2); [Yerushalmi Eruvin 9:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.9.4.2); Yoma chapter 4, halakhah 6; [Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 1:3:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shevuot.1.3.2) and [halakhah 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shevuot.1.6.5).[^5]

And it is possible that what they said in Niddah 15a, "Rabbi Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Yohanan," is this Rabbi Shmuel; but what we find in [Pesachim 112b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.112b.6), "Rabbi Shmuel said regarding a black ox," should, according to Hyman, read "Shmuel said," as in [Berakhot 33a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.33a.7); Dikdukei Soferim.[^2]
And we have already explained in the entry Shmuel that he too is sometimes called in the Yerushalmi by the name Rabbi Shmuel.[^4]

notes.text: רבע כארחיה means prostrating himself in his usual manner. Guggenheimer’s [Yerushalmi Avodah Zarah 4:1:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.4.1.5) discusses normal and sideways prostration and contains Rabbi Shmuel’s report about Rabbi Abbahu.
The identification of the Niddah speaker is only a possibility. The proposed correction in Pesachim and the cross-reference to the entry Shmuel are Hyman’s.
Hyman prints Shabbat 1:3; the corresponding passage is 1:6 in the linked edition.

The linked Pesachim names Rabbi Shmuel in the warning about the black ox. Berakhot names Shmuel, the form Hyman proposes for Pesachim. The matching Yochanan transmission is at [Niddah 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.15b.4), where the consulted text reads Rav Shmuel. Hyman supplies Niddah 15a and only tentatively connects its speaker with this Rabbi Shmuel. The chain in [Yerushalmi Yevamot 16:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.16.5.5) runs through Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Akiva bar Acha to Rabbi Yasa.
In Shevuot 1:3, Rabbi Shmuel cites Rabbi Zeira in an exposition of the word “their sins” in the laws of Yom Kippur.
